title: The upload that restarted from zero
blurb: Parts were marked stored before verification and the manifest double-counted.
prompt: A mobile client on a flaky network re-uploaded an entire multi-gigabyte file after one part failed, because the draft's resume endpoint returned only a percentage and the client had no choice. A double-registered part also inflated the byte accounting. Review it, fix it, and prove resume is part-exact.
aiNote: The draft marks each part stored when the store accepts the write, not when the checksum verifies, so corruption is found at finalize and costs a full re-upload, and its non-idempotent manifest registration lets a re-sent part inflate the byte count.
testIdea: Fail one part and assert only it is missing from the resume list; re-register the same part and assert the manifest bytes are unchanged; mark a part stored and then corrupt it and assert finalize fails with the part named.
followUps: What minimum part size keeps manifests sane?
How should resumable uploads work for mobile networks that change IPs?
When is server-side checksum verification too expensive?
